verdict.rationale: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol lets merchants cryptographically verify agent signatures and reject unsigned/invalid or replayed requests, and includes an agent-registry concept so merchants can 'confidently welcome agent-driven commerce while protecting your site from harmful bots' — a coarse allow/deny mechanism based on verified identity. However there is no documented per-agent or per-platform allow-list/deny-list management console, nor any rate-limiting feature for specific agents or platforms. Missing for 10: explicit merchant-facing controls to allow-list, deny-list, or throttle specific named agents/platforms (only signature-based legitimacy verification is evidenced), and independent confirmation of these controls in production use.
